technical-demo.title: Trading ideas evolve here.
technical-demo.caption: Trading ideas get lost in timelines and screenshots. An improvement should keep its own history.

technical-demo.title: A network of perspectives.
technical-demo.caption: FORK makes the idea the beginning of a conversation. The primary interaction is Fork, not a trade button.

technical-demo.title: Find an idea worth improving.
technical-demo.caption: Search real indexed perspectives by market, reasoning or author. This discovery window contains two ideas.

technical-demo.title: The original: thesis #1.
technical-demo.caption: A real author published an ETH long idea: target $4,200, invalidation $3,600 and leverage 2×.

technical-demo.title: Another author. Another approach.
technical-demo.caption: Fork #2 keeps the original parent and author while giving the contribution independent authorship.

technical-demo.title: The contribution is explicit.
technical-demo.caption: Target $4,200 → $4,400. Leverage 2× → 3×. Reasoning changes; invalidation and direction stay the same.

technical-demo.title: One idea. Many perspectives.
technical-demo.caption: The Idea Tree preserves the parent-child relationship. Every branch retains its author and origin.

technical-demo.title: Read the change in context.
technical-demo.caption: Compare the selected fork with its immediate parent, including both versions of the reasoning.

technical-demo.title: Keep the conversation visible.
technical-demo.caption: Root #1 already has one Agree and one comment. These offchain social actions are stored in PostgreSQL.

technical-demo.title: Reputation you can trace.
technical-demo.caption: Profiles explain Originality, Contribution and Influence. Small samples remain Emerging; no profit is implied.

technical-demo.title: Privy powers wallet authorship.
technical-demo.caption: This existing signed-in user retains the embedded wallet that authored thesis #1. Keys remain user-controlled.

technical-demo.title: A real Monad publication.
technical-demo.caption: The original transaction succeeded on Monad Testnet. This is existing proof, not a new transaction.

technical-demo.title: A real fork, indexed by Envio.
technical-demo.caption: The second wallet signed createThesis with parent #1. Envio indexes these registry events into the live social graph.

technical-demo.title: Trading ideas evolve here.
technical-demo.caption: Explore forktrades.xyz. Perpl and Nansen remain deferred; no trade execution is claimed.

founder-pitch.title: A better idea should not lose its credit.
founder-pitch.caption: Trading conversations create useful alternatives. Timelines make it hard to follow who contributed what.

founder-pitch.title: FORK / built by anilkaracay.
founder-pitch.caption: FORK is the social network where trading ideas evolve in public. Publish an idea, fork a better one, build its history.

founder-pitch.title: Give the improvement its own identity.
founder-pitch.caption: A fork preserves the original author and parent while making the new perspective independently attributable.

founder-pitch.title: The graph is the social product.
founder-pitch.caption: Readers discover ideas. Contributors build on them. The Idea Tree turns a conversation into persistent shared knowledge.

founder-pitch.title: Why Monad matters.
founder-pitch.caption: Monad records wallet authorship and lineage beyond one database. Fast, low-cost settlement suits frequent social contributions.

founder-pitch.title: Working proof, honest scale.
founder-pitch.caption: The deployed demo has two real users, one root and one fork, embedded wallets, live indexing, profiles and social interactions.

founder-pitch.title: Start with people who explain their ideas.
founder-pitch.caption: Our next step is an invited trader-community pilot: test whether people return to contribute useful alternatives. No traction is invented.

founder-pitch.title: Trading ideas evolve here.
founder-pitch.caption: Perpl execution and Nansen enrichment are deferred. No token or rewards are live. Explore the existing idea history at forktrades.xyz.
